Around each crossing choose a closed disk meeting the image in exactly two transverse arcs, with all such disks pairwise disjoint. Subdivide the remaining compact arcs into finitely many subarcs contained in planar coordinate disks where each arc is a graph over a line interval and where nonincident pieces are separated. Compactness and finiteness give a positive minimum for the separations between the disjoint pieces.

In each crossing disk, choose a nearby rational point $q$ and move the crossing there by a small planar isotopy supported in that disk. Choose four rational points on the four branch germs in the same cyclic order, and join each to $q$ by a rational straight segment; choose them close enough that the two lines through $q$ have nonzero determinant and stay in the same four sectors. Outside these disks, approximate each graph arc from step 1.1 by a sufficiently fine polygonal graph and perturb its finitely many vertices to rational coordinates. In each graph chart interpolate linearly between the original graph and the rational polygonal graph; the graphs remain embedded, their boundary endpoints agree, and their disjoint neighborhoods prevent new intersections. $$\widehat\gamma(t)=\bigl(\sqrt{1-a^2\cos^2(\pi t)}\,\gamma(t),\ a\cos(\pi t)\bigr),\qquad
